cron-fail-closed.ref: TWO CRONS, NO SCHEDULE CHANGE — both stop publishing fabricated numbers, and one of the three defects fixed here was mine from #1435. No job is added, removed, or re-tiered; every tier, interval, oncePerShopDay claim and gate is untouched.  1 · weeklyRevenueDigest — MARGIN WAS STILL FABRICATED AFTER #1435. That PR guarded on `costDetailCount > 0`, which is too weak: with ONE covered invoice out of 32 it still divided that invoice's parts by the FULL week's revenue and would have rendered ~99% — a fabrication with a guard in front of it. Margin is now computed over the covered subset only (coveredRevenue/coveredParts), and the rendered line quotes the COVERED parts/labor so the figures beside the margin share its basis; when coverage is partial the line names it ('on the 9/32 invoices carrying cost detail'). This matches the fill-guard already in services/engines/operations.ts rather than inventing a second pattern.  2 · revenue-reconciliation — HAS BEEN REPORTING $0 IN PROD. cron_log, last 8 days: '$0, 0 jobs' on 7 of them, against actual paid days of $806.75 / $1,554.95 / $3,772.22 / $2,873.28 / $2,008.96. Cause A: it called getDailyRevenueTruth() with NO argument — today so far — while sitting in the 24h tier whose phase follows pod boot (the ROS-081 class), so it fired at 11:59 / 14:03 / 16:01 / 19:08 / 21:18 UTC = 08:00-17:00 ET, before the day's invoices existed. Cause B, and the one that makes it harmful rather than merely wrong: nickMemory.remember() dedupes by CONTENT HASH, so every identical $0 message collapsed onto a single row — nick_memory_insight_e8bb1cbd7719 now carries **813 uses at confidence 1.0**, i.e. 'the shop made $0' is the most-reinforced revenue memory Nick holds, while real days sit at 1-6 uses. Repetition of a bug outvoted the truth. Fixed: reads the PREVIOUS COMPLETE shop day resolved in BUSINESS.timezone (not the container's UTC), stamps the date into the memory content so days can never pile up again, and writes NOTHING when the day has 0 jobs — a $0 day is a closed shop or a broken import, never a 'verified number'. FAIL-CLOSED BY DIRECTION: the job can now only ever write fewer, more-specific memories than before.  3 · getDailyRevenueTruth — published 100.0% margin every single day for 10 consecutive days (recomputed from prod), same root cause as #1435: ALG cost detail dead since 2026-04-09. Given the same subset-basis guard; grossMargin/grossMarginPercent are now nullable and the no-DB fallback returns null instead of a 0% margin, so a failed read cannot read as a measured one.  EVIDENCE: 31 tests (weeklyRevenueDigest 27, previousShopDay 4). MUTATION-VERIFIED ONE AT A TIME, each confirmed applied by grepping its anchor first and each source restored byte-identical after: (a) margin dividing by total revenue instead of coveredRevenue -> 1 failed / 26 passed; (b) quoting shop-wide parts beside the subset margin -> 1 failed; (c) printing zero-valued demand channels -> 1 failed; (d) resolving the reconciliation day in container TZ instead of shop TZ -> 1 failed / 3 passed. Broader surface: 16 files / 145 tests green across server/cron plus revenueAttribution, auto-invoice and adminPermissionCoverage. tsc --noEmit and typecheck:raw both 0 errors. Live re-preview after the fix renders the ALG-gap warning, a 1-entry top-services list, and 'Demand: 3 leads'.  NOT CLAIMED: the ALG importer is still broken — though its root cause is now IDENTIFIED, not unknown. Diagnosed from our own mirror and probe log with zero ALG contact: partsCost, laborCost AND taxAmount all fell to 0 together (2026-03: 77/110/67 of 134 -> 2026-04: 24/24/25 of 143 -> 2026-05: 0/0/0 of 104) while algTicketId and vehicleInfo stayed 100% populated. The three dead fields are exactly the flat line-item money fields mapRawInvoice reads (shopDriverMirror.ts:559-561); the two survivors are exactly what the code's own Wave-99 comment says /api/ticket/listRecentTickets returns. That endpoint is FIRST in the list and 'first one that returns data wins; we don't fall through', so the mirror is fed by a SUMMARY endpoint carrying no line-item split, and `!= null ? ... : 0` writes 0 silently. Wave-99's own probe (scripts/_archive/diagnose-line-items.ts) placed the line items on /api/ticket/listTicketSessions, which the import never reaches. The fix requires a per-ticket detail fetch — extra ALG traffic that collides with SHOP-PROTECT (scheduler.ts:517, probes evict the shop's login) — so it stays an operator decision, now with a price tag instead of a mystery. A warning block at the mapper and a full write-up in docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md prevent the next reader from re-deriving it. The 813-use poisoned memory row also STILL EXISTS — deleting it is a prod write and an operator decision. Neither cron has yet run in production under this change. Both recorded in docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md. Prior entry (#1435 margin fix) superseded per the rolling-manifest rule.

cron-fail-closed-superseded-1435.ref: THIS DIFF ADDS NO JOB AND REMOVES NONE — it stops one existing cron from PUBLISHING A FABRICATED NUMBER. weeklyRevenueDigest is scheduled but has never fired (first firing Mon 2026-08-10 ET); the schedule entry, tier, oncePerShopDay claim and Monday gate are all untouched.  HOW IT WAS FOUND — the operator said fire it now. A read-only preview (scripts/preview-weekly-digest.mts, SELECTs only, no send path) run against the live mirror rendered: 'Parts $0 · Labor $0 · Margin 100%' on $16,656.95 of real revenue across 32 paid invoices, and a top-services list whose #1 row was '(no description)' holding $15,855 — 97% of the money. Both are fabrications and BOTH PASSED 18 GREEN TESTS, because every fixture assumed populated columns. The tests exercised the arithmetic and never asserted it against reality.  THE UNDERLYING PRODUCTION FACT, probed live and independently of this job: ALG invoice cost detail stopped arriving on 2026-04-09. Of 2,899 lifetime paid invoices, 1,886 carry partsCost and 1,871 carry laborCost — but 0 of the last 30 do. Monthly withParts: Mar 77/134, Apr 24/143, May 0/104, Jun 0/123, Jul 0/106, Aug 0/30. serviceDescription is degrading on the same curve (Jun 31/123, Jul 12/106, Aug 1/30). With partsCost pinned at 0, `revenue - partsCost` equals revenue, so the naive margin formula returns exactly 100% — for a tire shop that plainly buys parts.  FAIL-CLOSED, APPLIED TO DATA RATHER THAN TO ERRORS. The existing failure posture (any thrown query suppresses the whole send; ER_BAD_FIELD/TABLE/PARSE reports SCHEMA BUG) is unchanged and still covered, including the late-query cases added last commit. What this diff adds is the same principle one level up: a query that SUCCEEDS and returns nothing must not render as good news. marginPct is now null unless costDetailCount > 0, the text names the gap ('Parts/labor missing on all N invoices — margin unavailable (ALG import gap)') instead of printing a number, partial coverage is labelled 'cost detail on N/M', and top services queries only described rows and says 'unavailable' when there are none rather than ranking the absence of data.  EVIDENCE: 5 tests added (23 total, up from 18) — margin never rendered at zero cost detail (asserts the string 'Margin' is ABSENT, not merely different), partial-coverage labelling, top-services unavailable line, description-coverage display, and a compute-layer test that marginPct is null on the exact prod shape (32 invoices, $16,656.95, 0 cost detail). MUTATION-VERIFIED against the precise regression: restoring the unguarded `revenue > 0 ? ...` margin turns exactly one test RED (1 failed / 22 passed); the mutation was confirmed applied by grepping its anchor, and the source restored byte-identical afterwards (md5 2a77f7c6d04d0971fc73cfc64074f2fb on backup and restored file), 23/23 green after restore. Re-running the live preview post-fix renders the warning line and a 1-entry top-services list with '(described: 1/32)'.  NOT CLAIMED, and this is the important part: THE IMPORTER IS NOT FIXED. Why ALG stopped sending parts/labor/description is unknown; ALG is read-only by operator directive so diagnosing it is not this PR's to do. Recorded in docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md as an operator call, together with the note that getDailyRevenueTruth and the parts-percent outlier scan in services/engines/operations.ts consume the same columns and have NOT been reviewed — they may be publishing the same artifact. Still no production run of the cron itself. Prior entry (demand-line late-query coverage, #1433) superseded per the rolling-manifest rule.

cron-fail-closed-superseded-1433.ref: THIS DIFF ADDS NO JOB AND REMOVES NONE — it changes what ONE existing cron READS. weeklyRevenueDigest (added #1427, has never fired; first firing Mon 2026-08-10 ET) gains two demand queries: lead rows, and a funnel count over bookings + callback_requests. The schedule entry in cron/scheduler.ts is untouched — same hourly tier, same oncePerShopDay claim, same shop-TZ Monday gate. No job gains the ability to run and none loses it.  THE FAIL-CLOSED CLAIM, AND WHY THE NEW QUERIES CHANGE ITS SHAPE. The two additions run FIFTH and SIXTH, after all four revenue queries have already succeeded. That creates a partial-result hazard the job did not have when every query was about money: revenue would render correctly while the demand line silently read `0 leads · 0 bookings · 0 callbacks` — which on a phone reads as a DEAD WEEK, not as a failed read. That is strictly worse than sending nothing, and it is the exact 'all-clear on failure' class this repo has paid for repeatedly. Both queries therefore sit inside the same try that wraps computeWeeklyRevenueDigest, so any throw suppresses the ENTIRE send and writes the reason to cron_log; the #1125 schema-error taxonomy (ER_BAD_FIELD/TABLE/PARSE -> 'SCHEMA BUG') applies at any query position, not just the first.  EVIDENCE — and the previous test file did NOT cover this. The pre-existing failure test rejected the FIRST query, which proves nothing about a throw that happens after four successes. Two tests added: (1) the 5th query (lead rows) throws after four successes -> sendTelegram not called, recordsProcessed 0, details 'digest failed'; (2) the 6th query (funnel) throws ER_BAD_FIELD_ERROR -> reported as SCHEMA BUG, proving the taxonomy does not degrade with query position.  MUTATION-VERIFIED, and the mutation is the precise regression these guard: wrapping the lead query in a local try/catch that swallows the error and leaves leads=0 — i.e. someone 'defensively' making the demand line resilient — turns test (1) RED (1 failed / 17 passed) while everything else stays green. The mutation was confirmed APPLIED by grepping its anchor before the run (a mutation that silently fails to apply looks exactly like a passing test), and the source was restored byte-identical afterwards: md5 c1fce572c980e4b08e6d148db8dc0b7e on both the backup and the restored file, 18/18 green after restore.  Also verified: the demand line reuses the SHARED countActionableLeads rather than COUNT(*), so this cron cannot drift from dailyReport's lead definition — pinned by a 4-row fixture containing one callback-linked duplicate that must yield 3.  NOT CLAIMED: no production run. The job has never executed; every assertion above is against fixtures and a mutation, not a live Monday send. Prior entry (cross-sell-outreach schedule removal, #1355-era) superseded per the rolling-manifest rule.

operator-walkthrough.ref: WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES — one MORE line in Monday's Telegram digest, and one admin API that was never reachable is gone. THE FINDING: `weeklyReport.generate` was registered in the tRPC tree (routers.ts:153) and had ZERO callers — `grep -rn weeklyReport client/` returns nothing, no cron references it, and the only other hits were the router's own file plus two test fixtures listing its name. `notifyWeeklyReport` in email-notify.ts was identically dead: the sole reference was auto-invoice.test.ts asserting `typeof === 'function'` — a test that proved the export existed and nothing more. So a 'weekly intelligence report' existed in code, was documented, was permission-checked, and had never once run.  WHY THIS IS A COLLAPSE, NOT A DELETION. The tempting read is 'nobody clicked it, nobody wants it'. The evidence says otherwise: it required clicking, and this operator consumes pushed reports (daily SMS, Telegram digests) and no pull-only ones. What went unused was the TRANSPORT, not the content — the same finding that made the revenue digest a push in #1427. So its content moves to the live pushed job: `Demand: N leads · N bookings · N callbacks (N still open)`, where unworked callbacks are the actionable half.  ★ A CONSISTENCY TRAP CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED. The obvious implementation is `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM leads`. That would have made this report DISAGREE with the daily one: dailyReport.ts:48 counts leads through `countActionableLeads` (shared/leadSource.ts), which excludes a `source='callback'` lead carrying a `callbackId` because that row and its callback_requests row are the SAME PERSON. A raw count double-counts them. Re-expressing that predicate in SQL would have forked a definition the repo deliberately centralized, so the digest fetches the rows and calls the shared function — one definition, no drift. A test pins it: a 4-row lead fixture containing exactly one callback-linked duplicate must yield 3, and the comment says out loud that a reading of 4 means someone re-implemented the rule in SQL.  EVIDENCE: weeklyRevenueDigest.test.ts now 16 tests (3 new: the shared-rule lead count, the demand line, and the open-callbacks callout suppressed at zero). Serial run of the three touched files: 3 files / 68 tests passed, exit 0. tsc --noEmit exit 0 WITH the router deleted — the compiler confirms nothing referenced it. validate:routes ✓ ('every App.tsx route is registered'). lint:source ✓.  NOT CLAIMED: the digest has still never fired in production — first firing is Monday 2026-08-10 business hours ET, and the demand line is asserted against fixtures, not a live send. No admin UI changed, because the deleted procedure had no UI to change.

WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES — nothing on Instagram, which is how this was found. The operator asked why autonomous reels had stopped; production said the rest.  ★ ONE — A BILLING WALL FILED AS A TRANSIENT BLIP. Reel job #1380001 (2026-08-04 18:03, cron) failed with Higgsfield's grace_daily_limit_reached / unlock_full_access_notice. That text matched NONE of the eight classifier patterns — no "billing", no "exhausted", and no "rate" for RATE_LIMIT — so it fell through to UNKNOWN, whose policy is RETRY_BACKOFF and whose operator-facing reason literally reads "unrecognised failure - treated as transient, but review the message". The daily cron re-attempted every day and NOTHING alerted. It now classifies as QUOTA_OR_CREDIT -> PAUSE_PROVIDER, which stops the lane and raises a human.  Deliberately NOT RATE_LIMIT, and the difference is money: RATE_LIMIT is RETRY_WITHOUT_CONSUMING_ATTEMPT, built for a request refused before work began that clears on its own. A grace-tier daily cap does not clear by waiting and cannot be retried out of - it needs a plan upgrade. A test asserts it is not that class.  ★ THE TEST CAUGHT A TRAP IN MY OWN FIX. The first draft appended the new wordings to the existing QUOTA_OR_CREDIT regex, which is wrapped in  ... . `_` is a WORD character, so   never fires inside an underscore-joined token:  grace[_ ]daily[_ ]limit  does NOT match "grace_daily_limit_reached", because the boundary it wants sits between `limit` and `_reached` with word characters on both sides. Three cases went red. The plan-wall patterns are now their own entry and the working credit regex is untouched.  ★ TWO — A TRUNCATED RESPONSE REPORTED AS A BACKTICK. ig_autopost_log carried `Unexpected token '`', "```json
{"... is not valid JSON` (2026-08-05) and `Unterminated string in JSON at position 830` (2026-08-01). Both are ONE root cause - the model's output was cut off mid-object - and neither message says so; the first names the backtick, which is the only detail that does not matter. parseJsonObject now detects an opening brace with no closing one and throws `LLM response truncated before the JSON object closed (N chars received) - raise max_tokens for this call`, and wraps genuine syntax errors instead of leaking the raw parser text into a column the operator reads.  ★ AND A MUTATION PROVED PART OF MY OWN FIX DEAD. The draft also stripped an UNCLOSED fence. Disabling that line changed no behaviour: the brace isolation already recovers the object whenever one closed, and when none closed the truncation branch fires first either way. It was removed rather than kept with a comment claiming it fixed the prod error. The surviving branch is verified load-bearing - disabling it turns 2 cases red.  EVIDENCE: server/providerErrorAndLlmJsonTruth.test.ts (10), built from the EXACT prod stderr payload rather than a paraphrase, MUTATION-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS - removing the plan-wall pattern (3 red) · reclassifying it as RATE_LIMIT (4 red) · disabling the truncation branch (2 red) · deleting the truncation message (1 red). One further mutation SURVIVED and that is why a line was deleted; the first attempt at it silently failed to apply and reported a false pass, so the applied ones are proven by echoing the removed text and by git diff --stat. A regression case pins that the other six error classes are unchanged. Full serial suite: 405 files passed / 2 skipped, 4,981 passed / 50 skipped / 1 todo, exit 0. tsc --noEmit clean.  NOT CLAIMED: neither fix makes a reel. The Higgsfield account is behind a plan-tier daily cap - an operator billing action - and this change only makes that state stop the lane loudly instead of retrying it silently. No production run has exercised either path since the change; the classification is asserted against the recorded payload, not against a new live failure.

render-spend-trajectory.ref: THIS DIFF CHANGES SPEND, and the change is downward and bounded. The rule fires on server/services/reelPipeline.ts, which is where render spend is both reserved and settled, so here is the whole trajectory.  BEFORE: a paid provider returning a verdict no retry can clear (QUOTA_OR_CREDIT, AUTH_INVALID -> PAUSE_PROVIDER) sent the job terminal. Spend for the remaining beats: zero, because nothing rendered - and no reel either. AFTER, and only when REEL_FALLBACK_TO_TEMPLATE_STOCK=true: the remaining beats render on the local ffmpeg lane. Spend for those beats is still zero (reelClipCostUsd('template_stock') is 0 and the lane makes no provider call - templateStockStudio.ts contains exactly one fetch, a download of an already-hosted hero image), and now there IS a reel. No path in this diff can increase spend: the flip is one-way and only ever moves from a paid lane to the free one, never the reverse.  ★ THE REAL FINDING, and it is a defect this change would otherwise have INTRODUCED. Settlement read `clipUrls.length * reelClipCostUsd(videoProvider)`, and the comment directly above it warns that settling at a flat rate is 'what made a mid-flight provider flip undetectable in the ledger, and would settle a free local reel as if it had spent Seedance money'. Introducing a mid-job flip made videoProvider stop being the provider that actually rendered, so a degraded reel would have billed every clip at the paid rate - resurrecting the exact bug already fixed once on the repair lane (#1343, where a hardcoded seedance1_5 filed template_stock repairs under Higgsfield's name). The reserve() call at enqueue anticipates this in writing: 'a mid-flight provider flip can still diverge - settlement is where actuals must be reconciled.' Settlement now splits the bill: paidClips * reelClipCostUsd(videoProvider) + freeLaneClips * reelClipCostUsd('template_stock'), where freeLaneClips counts what the free lane actually rendered this run. With no flip freeLaneClips is 0 and the expression is arithmetically identical to the original, so unflipped jobs settle exactly as before.  The reservation itself is UNTOUCHED: still created at enqueue against the selected provider at beatsCount * reelClipCostUsd(reservedProvider), still checked against the daily ceiling.
